name: ForceDream

hlido_opinion.headline: Extraordinary claims — 99.97% uptime SLA, 4.2M+ sealed events, 78% margin "enforced in code", 90 settlement corridors — with a verification link as the only offered proof and no operating history behind any of it.
hlido_opinion.body: ForceDream presents itself as a "sovereign intelligence operating system for the global agentic economy": multi-provider inference arbitrage, an immutable SHA-256 WORM audit chain sealed from genesis, 78% of margin to developers enforced cryptographically before the response returns, autonomous agent payments, and 90 settlement corridors across 166 currencies with African mobile-money rails in development. The density and specificity of the numbers is the problem rather than the reassurance: **330+ live routes, 100% rule-enforced, 78% developer earnings, 99.97% uptime SLA, 4.2M+ WORM events, −43.2% inference cost, 117ms latency**, plus a live-updating genesis hash. Any one of these would be a significant claim; together, from an entity with no named team, no company details, no customers, no case studies and no operating history on the surface we captured, they form a pattern that warrants caution rather than confidence. A 99.97% uptime SLA is a contractual commitment, and no terms are shown. "78% of margin enforced in code" is checkable in principle — the page offers a genesis endpoint and a "verify live" link — and we credit that the mechanism is at least pointed at; but a self-published hash verifies internal consistency, not that the accounting behind it is honest or that the money moves as described. Cross-border settlement across 166 currencies is a regulated activity in most jurisdictions, and no licensing or regulatory posture is stated anywhere. We are not asserting anything here is false — we could not verify any of it, which is precisely the finding. The score records unverifiable extraordinary claims, and would move substantially on audited figures or named customers.

tier_rationale: FADING (50) because the surface pairs extraordinary, highly specific claims (99.97% uptime SLA, 4.2M+ sealed events, −43.2% inference cost, 90 settlement corridors across 166 currencies) with no team, no company details, no customers, no operating history, and no regulatory posture for what is described as cross-border settlement. Self-published cryptographic verification demonstrates internal consistency, not honest accounting. This scores absence of verifiable substantiation behind unusually strong claims — not a finding that any specific claim is false.
what_it_does_well: Points at a verification mechanism (public genesis endpoint, live hash) rather than asking for pure trust
Immutable WORM audit chain sealed before the billable response returns is a sound architectural idea
Developer revenue share stated as a specific, checkable number rather than a vague promise
Multi-provider inference arbitrage is a real and useful optimisation
Explicit that mobile-money rails are 'in development' rather than claiming them as live
what_it_fails_at: No named team, company details, jurisdiction, or operating history anywhere on the surface
A 99.97% uptime SLA is asserted with no terms, no status page history, and no contract shown
Headline figures (4.2M+ WORM events, −43.2% inference cost, 117ms latency, 330+ routes) are unaudited and unverifiable
Cross-border settlement across 166 currencies is regulated activity; no licensing or regulatory posture stated
No customers, case studies, or third-party validation of any kind
Cryptographic sealing proves internal consistency, not that the underlying accounting is honest
Very high claim density relative to available evidence
best_for: Nobody we can identify from the public surface without substantially more disclosure
not_recommended_for: Anyone routing production inference or money through it on the strength of this page
Buyers with vendor due-diligence requirements — the basic disclosures are absent
Developers relying on the 78% margin commitment without contractual terms
Any regulated context requiring a known, licensed counterparty

red_flags.note: A 99.97% uptime SLA is advertised with no terms, no status history and no identifiable contracting entity. An SLA from an anonymous operator is not an SLA.

Cross-border settlement across 90 corridors and 166 currencies is described as live. This is regulated activity in most jurisdictions and no licensing, registration or regulatory posture appears anywhere on the surface.

Cryptographic sealing and a public genesis hash are offered as proof of the 78% margin commitment. They can demonstrate that records were not altered after the fact; they cannot demonstrate that the accounting entered into them is correct.
